page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture AMD EPYC 7H12 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.g6a.large exhibits lower-tier performance across most compute and memory metrics. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with the PassMark CPU score, place the instance in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance, with read-only large block transfers at 23.06 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 15.78 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 25%. However, single-threaded performance shows some resilience, with Geekbench single-core scores and bzip3 single-threaded decompression rates achieving average tier results.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but modest dual-core configuration, the instance offers a predictable but limited performance profile. It lacks advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX, though it supports standard AVX, AES, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions. The absence of local storage and GPUs, combined with poor database and Redis SET benchmark results, makes it less suitable for high-throughput database operations or heavy data processing. The instance is best positioned for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, or development environments where dedicated CPU resources are required without demanding high memory or compute throughput.
